summary: On Yom Tov we should carry things in a different way than on a weekday. And which straw and wood may we take for the fire?

chunks.en: Someone who brings jugs of wine from one place to another
chunks.st: One who brings wine jugs from one place to another place

chunks.en: may not bring them in a basket or a box,
chunks.explain: That is the weekday way of carrying many jugs.
chunks.st: may not bring a large number of them in a basket or in a tub
chunks.stMore: in the usual weekday manner on a Festival, as this is disrespectful of the Festival;

chunks.he: אֲבָל מֵבִיא הוּא עַל כְּתֵפוֹ אוֹ לְפָנָיו.
chunks.en: but he may carry them on his shoulder or in front of him.
chunks.st: but he may bring one or two barrels on his shoulder or carry them in front of himself.

chunks.en: And so, someone who carries straw
chunks.st: Similarly, one who brings straw
chunks.stMore: for kindling or for feeding animals

chunks.en: may not swing the box onto his back,
chunks.st: may not place the tub behind him
chunks.stMore: while carrying it, as this is the usual weekday manner;

chunks.en: but he may carry it in his hand.
chunks.st: but he may transport it in front of him in his hand,
chunks.stMore: in an unusual fashion.

chunks.en: We may start taking straw from a pile,
chunks.st: And one may begin taking straw for kindling from the pile of straw,
chunks.stMore: although he did not designate the pile for this purpose the day before;

chunks.en: but not from the wood in the storage yard.
chunks.st: but one may not begin to take from the wood in the wood storage, a small yard behind the house where people store various items that they do not intend to use in the near future.

words.en: that is in the storage yard

summary: Which wood may we take for the fire on Yom Tov? Not from a sukkah, and only from wood that was ready from before Yom Tov.

chunks.en: We may not take wood from a sukkah,
chunks.explain: Taking it would be like breaking down a building.
chunks.st: One may not take wood from a sukka
chunks.stMore: on any Festival, not only on the festival of Sukkot, because this is considered dismantling,

chunks.en: only from what is next to it.
chunks.st: but one may take from near it.

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין עֵצִים מִן הַשָּׂדֶה מִן הַמְכֻנָּס,
chunks.en: We may bring wood from a field only from a pile,
chunks.st: One may bring wood chopped from a tree the previous day from an unfenced field, but only from that which has been gathered
chunks.stMore: into a pile before the Festival for the purpose of using it for kindling. However, scattered wood is muktze and may not be handled.

chunks.en: and from a karpef, even wood that is scattered.
chunks.st: And if one brings wood from a karpef used for storage, he may bring even from the scattered wood,
chunks.stMore: as it is considered a guarded courtyard rather than a field, and one does not remove even scattered items from his mind if they are stored inside such an enclosure.

words.note: A fenced yard used for keeping things.

chunks.en: What is a karpef?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: What is a karpef?

chunks.en: Any one near the city.
chunks.st: It is any enclosure that is near a city, but if it is far from a city, it is considered a field;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Any one that we go into with a key,
chunks.st: Any fenced place into which one can enter only with a key is a karpef, even if it is located at a distance from a city,

chunks.en: as long as it is within the techum Shabbos.
chunks.st: provided that it is within the Shabbat limit.

words.note: The limit of how far we may walk out of town on Shabbos.

summary: How may we chop wood on Yom Tov? And may we take fruit out of a closed storeroom that has a hole?

chunks.en: We may not chop wood
chunks.st: One may not chop wood

chunks.en: from building beams,
chunks.st: on a Festival neither from beams intended for construction

chunks.he: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: or from a beam that broke on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: nor from a beam that broke on a Festival,
chunks.stMore: although it no longer serves any purpose.

chunks.en: And we may not chop with an ax,
chunks.st: And one may not chop wood on a Festival, neither with an ax,

chunks.en: or with a saw, or with a sickle,
chunks.st: nor with a saw, nor with a sickle,
chunks.stMore: as these are clearly craftsman’s tools used on weekdays.

chunks.en: only with a cleaver.
chunks.st: Rather, one may chop only with a cleaver.
chunks.stMore: Using this tool differs greatly from the weekday manner in which wood is chopped.

chunks.en: A storeroom full of fruit
chunks.st: If there is a house that is filled with produce

chunks.en: that was closed up and a hole opened in it:
chunks.st: and locked on all sides, and a hole formed in one of its walls or its roof,

chunks.en: he may take fruit out through the hole.
chunks.st: one may remove produce through the place of the hole.
chunks.stMore: The produce is not considered muktze, even though one cannot reach it without the existence of the hole.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: He may even make a hole from the start and take fruit.
chunks.st: One may even make a hole ab initio and take produce through that opening.

summary: On Yom Tov we may not make a new lamp, make charcoal, or cut a wick with a knife.

chunks.en: We may not shape a clay lamp on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: On a Festival, one may not hollow out a piece of clay to form a lamp
chunks.stMore: into which he will place oil and a wick

chunks.en: because he is making a new vessel.
chunks.st: because he thereby creates a vessel.

chunks.en: We may not make charcoal on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not produce charcoal at all on a Festival
chunks.stMore: because this is not labor for sustenance.

chunks.en: and we may not cut a wick in two.
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not cut the wick,
chunks.stMore: as this is considered mending a vessel.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He may cut it with fire, for two lamps.
chunks.explain: He lights it in the middle, between two lamps.
chunks.st: If one requires a wick of a particular length, he may cut it by burning it in a fire but not by cutting it with a knife.
chunks.basisNote: How it is done follows Bartenura.

summary: More things we may not do on Yom Tov, because they are like weekday work or like building.

chunks.en: We may not break a piece of clay on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not break earthenware on a Festival.

chunks.en: and we may not cut paper
chunks.st: And one may not cut paper

chunks.en: to roast salted fish on it.
chunks.st: in order to roast salted fish on it.
chunks.stMore: Earthenware shards or pieces of paper that have been soaked in water were placed on the metal surface or in the oven in which the fish was roasted, so that it would not be burned by the heat.

chunks.en: We may not sweep out an oven or a stove,
chunks.st: And one may not sweep out anything that has fallen into an oven or stove that interferes with the baking, such as plaster.

chunks.en: but we may press down the ashes.
chunks.st: But one may press down
chunks.stMore: and flatten any accumulated dust and ashes at the bottom of the oven, which might prevent it from lighting properly.

chunks.en: We may not put two barrels next to each other
chunks.st: And one may not draw two barrels together

chunks.en: to put a pot on top of them,
chunks.st: in order to place a pot on them,
chunks.stMore: so that its contents will be cooked by a fire lit between the barrels.

chunks.en: We may not prop up a pot with a piece of wood,
chunks.st: And one may not prop a pot that does not stand straight with a piece of wood,
chunks.stMore: in order to prevent it from falling.

chunks.en: and the same with a door.
chunks.st: And similarly, with a door.

chunks.en: We may not lead an animal
chunks.st: And one may not lead an animal

chunks.en: with a stick on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: with a stick in the public domain on a Festival;

chunks.en: and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon allows it.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permits it.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages argue about which bits of wood or straw we may take on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: A person may take a little stick from what is in front of him
chunks.st: On a Festival, a person may remove a sliver from a pile of straw or from similar material that is before him,

words.en: from what is in front of him

chunks.en: to clean his teeth with it.
chunks.st: in order to clean with it between his teeth.

chunks.en: And he may gather sticks from the yard and light them,
chunks.st: And he may collect straw from a courtyard and kindle it,

chunks.en: because everything in the yard is ready to be used.
chunks.st: for anything in a courtyard is considered prepared for all purposes.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: The Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He may gather only from what is in front of him, and light it.
chunks.st: He may collect these materials only from things placed before him in his house, as they are certainly prepared for all uses, and kindle them.
chunks.stMore: With regard to objects lying in his courtyard, however, as their collection takes great effort, he certainly did not have them in mind the day before, and they are therefore muktze.

words.en: from what is in front of him

summary: We may not make a new fire on Yom Tov. Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages also argue about how to pick out fruit before Shabbos to eat on Shabbos.

chunks.en: We may not make a new fire on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: The mishna states a different halakha: One may not produce fire,

chunks.en: not from wood,
chunks.st: neither from wood, by rubbing one piece against another;

chunks.en: not from stones,
chunks.st: nor from stones knocked against each other;

chunks.en: not from earth,
chunks.st: nor from hot dirt;
chunks.stMore: nor from tiles struck against each other;

chunks.en: and not from water.
chunks.explain: Water in a glass can focus the sun and start a fire.
chunks.st: nor from water
chunks.stMore: placed in round, glass vessels, which produces fire by focusing the rays of the sun.

chunks.he: וְאֵין מְלַבְּנִין אֶת הָרְעָפִים לִצְלוֹת בָּהֶן.
chunks.en: We may not heat tiles very hot to roast on them.
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not whiten tiles with a burning-hot heat in order to roast upon them afterward.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer also said:
chunks.st: And Rabbi Eliezer further stated the following leniency:

chunks.en: A person may stand by the place where his fruit is drying
chunks.st: A person may stand over objects in storage,
chunks.stMore: such as produce that he has for some reason previously set aside from use,

words.note: Where fruit is spread out to dry.

chunks.en: on Friday, in the Shemitah year,
chunks.st: on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year,
chunks.stMore: during which no tithes are separated, which means one may take fruit on the following day without the need for any corrective measure,

chunks.en: and say: I will eat from here tomorrow.
chunks.st: and say: From here, from these fruits, I will eat tomorrow.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Only if he marks it and says:
chunks.st: He may not eat unless he marks the pile of fruit the day before and explicitly says:

chunks.en: From here until there.
chunks.st: From here to there I will take.
